newsitem.title: UK: Telewest says mulls NTL approach.
newsitem.headline: Telewest says mulls NTL approach.

text.p: British cable TV company Telewest Communications Plc confirmed on Monday it had been approached by Nasdaq-listed NTL Inc about a joint deal and said it was considering the proposal.
But the company stressed that any talks were at a very early stage.
"There has been an approach and we are looking at it as we look at any other approach," a spokesman told Reuters.

The spokesman declined to comment on the nature of the approach, but newspapers have said that NTL wants to merge with Telewest to create a 1.0 billion pound ($1.6 billion) rival to the country's biggest cable television and telephone giant -- Cable and Wireless Communications.
Amid increasing consolidation in the cable industry, Telewest has said that there are always discussions with cable companies and other media groups both in Britain and in America.

But the company said it could shed no light on newspaper reports that United News & Media Plc, one of Britain's three largest commercial television operators, planned to move into cable TV by taking a big minority stake in any new cable company.
Both United News and NTL, which was formed from the acquisition of National Transcommunications Ltd by International CableTel in March 1996, declined to comment.
Telewest, whose shares rose 6.0p to 85p, lost its position as Britain's biggest cable operator after Cable and Wireless Communications (CWC) was formed by a complex four-way merger earlier this year.
CWC brought together Cable and Wireless Plc's Mercury telephone subsidiary and the British cable TV units of NYNEX Corp and Bell Canada -- NYNEX CableComms Group Bell Cablemedia Plc and Videotron.
